headline.fallback: The quarter in numbers for {{ account.name }}

next_note.fallback: Pick a time and we will go through these numbers together and agree the plan for next quarter.

recipe.prompt:
You are writing the prose of a quarterly value review for {{ account.name }} ({{ account.domain }}). It is sent by {{ sender.name | default: 'the account owner' }} at {{ brand.name | default: 'our company' }} to {{ person.first_name | default: 'the team' }} {{ person.last_name | default: '' }}. "We" and "us" mean {{ brand.name | default: 'our company' }}. Sender title: {{ sender.title | default: 'none' }}. Person title: {{ person.title | default: 'none' }}.

Input: data.rows, the usage export for this account. Every row has kind and label. kind is one of:
- quarter: label is the quarter, like "Q3 2026". hours_saved, active_seats, seats (seats on the contract), tasks_done and median_hours are that quarter's totals. detail is the period in words. Rows are oldest first. The last quarter row is this quarter and the one before it is last quarter.
- month: label is the month, quarter is the quarter it belongs to, active_seats is the seats active that month, detail is an optional note on what happened.
- team: label is the team, seats is the seats assigned, active_seats is the seats active, hours_saved is the hours the team saved this quarter, detail says what the team does with the product.
- milestone: label and date (YYYY-MM-DD) and an optional detail. marker is start (contract start), review (this review) or renewal (the renewal date). Milestones dated after the review milestone are still ahead.
If data.rows holds no quarter row, return {} and nothing else.

Write JSON with all of these keys. When the rows do not give you what a key needs, return it empty: "" for a string, [] for a list.
- headline: one sentence of 60 to 160 characters. What the account got this quarter: hours saved, the change against last quarter in whole percent, and active seats out of seats. Like "Brightwave Logistics saved 1,840 hours in Q3, 22 percent more than in Q2, with 96 of 120 seats active." Leave out the comparison when there is no last quarter.
- usage_note: 1 or 2 sentences, at most 300 characters, on the month rows: where active seats started, where they are now, and one month's note from detail if there is one. Say "grew every month" only when each month is higher than the one before. Return "" with fewer than 2 month rows.
- adoption_note: 1 or 2 sentences, at most 300 characters, on the team rows: which teams are close to full use and how many seats are not yet active in the others. Return "" when there are no team rows.
- wins: up to 3 items {stat, unit, title, body, team}, one per team, the teams with the most hours_saved. stat is that team's hours_saved with a comma for thousands, like "1,480". unit is "hours". title is "Hours saved by <team label>". body is 1 or 2 sentences, at most 280 characters: the team's detail, then how many of its seats are active. team is "<team label>, <active_seats> of <seats> seats". If no team has hours_saved, pick the teams with the most active seats and use that number as stat with unit "active seats". Return [] when there are no team rows.
- plan: 1 to 4 items {when, what, who} for next quarter, in date order. Base each on one milestone dated after the review milestone (skip the renewal milestone) or on the seats not yet active, which is seats minus active_seats in this quarter's row. when is the milestone date written like "5 Nov 2026", or "Next quarter" when there is no date. what is one sentence of at most 200 characters from the milestone's label and detail. who is the people on the task: "{{ person.first_name | default: 'none' }} {{ person.last_name | default: '' }}, {{ sender.name | default: 'none' }}" when both attend, the sender's name alone for a task on our side, and "{{ account.name }} team" in place of the person when the person is none. Return [] when there is nothing ahead.
- next_note: 2 or 3 sentences, at most 360 characters. Name the one thing to settle before the renewal date, taken from the milestones, then ask them to book a time to go through the plan. With no milestones, only ask them to book a time to go through the numbers and the plan.

Facts: every number comes from data.rows, or is a plain difference or a whole-percent change between two numbers in it. Never invent customers, people, causes, dates, tools, quotes or results. Do not say why a number moved unless a detail says so. Do not name anyone except the people in the inputs.

Voice: one person writing to a peer about their account. Plain, specific, short sentences. Sentence case. Write "percent", not the percent sign.

Rules for every string: no em dashes or en dashes. No exclamation marks. No email addresses or phone numbers. No hype words (unlock, leverage, seamless, robust, crucial, elevate, delve, transform, game changer, cutting-edge). Never "real" as emphasis.

recipe.rubric:
Grade the headline, usage_note, adoption_note, wins, plan and next_note of a quarterly value review for {{ account.name }} against data.rows. 10 is copy a customer reads once and trusts.
Score these, 0 to 10 each:
- accurate: every number matches data.rows, or is a plain difference or whole-percent change between two of its numbers. Seats and hours belong to the right team and the right quarter. Any number that is not in the rows fails the page.
- grounded: nothing is claimed that the rows and their detail columns do not say. No invented reasons, customers, people, dates or promises. A plan row traces to a milestone or to the seats not yet active.
- plain: short sentences, specific facts, sentence case, no hype, no filler. Wins read as three different teams.
Answer yes or no:
- weird_word: is there a phrase a person would not say out loud (jargon, marketing adjectives, stacked nouns)? Quote it.
Automatic fail: an em dash or en dash, an exclamation mark, an email address or phone number, a percent sign, or a sign-off or name at the end of next_note.
